title: Parallel proof search by twenty-plus coordinated agents
text: Splits a Putnam-level math problem across an orchestrator and more than twenty parallel sub-agents that subscribe to task state and share intermediate discoveries while a proof is built.

title: Swarm shipping 127 pull requests in a weekend
text: Runs eighteen specialised agents through research, planning, design review, implementation, security audit and CI monitoring, with deterministic quality checks between phases, merging 127 pull requests to production in one weekend.

title: Terminal dashboard managing a hundred coding agents
text: Manages a large fleet of coding agents from one terminal dashboard, letting agents supervise other agents hierarchically like a company org chart.

title: Fleet of coding agents on a task database
text: Runs ten to fifteen coding agents at once from a Python orchestrator and shared task database with dependencies, then investigates where usage limits go to trim consumption.

title: Research repository coordinated by planner and workers
text: Coordinates several coding agents on one research project by using the repository itself as shared memory, with a planner scoping tasks with explicit ownership boundaries.

title: Swarm of puzzle-playing agents on ARC-AGI-3
text: Launches many competing agents that each play abstract reasoning puzzle games from a plain-English strategy prompt, self-reflect on results, and post scores to a shared leaderboard.

title: Autonomous startup run by fourteen persona agents
text: Loops fourteen agents with executive personas through repeated cycles around one shared consensus file, building a landing page, Docker stack, release and community posts with rare human escalation.

title: Debate between coding assistants before an answer
text: Lets two different coding assistants each analyse a request, debate approaches, then synthesise one solution, using personas such as architect, debugger and security expert.

title: Deliberate, council and debate modes across assistants
text: Orchestrates several coding assistants in modes where one drafts and another reviews to consensus, several give parallel opinions with anonymous ranking, or two argue pro and con before a judge.

title: Company-style team of terminal agents with contracts
text: Runs separate command-line agents as a company team that publish API contracts and require sign-offs before coding, communicating through a central message hub with idle-aware queues.

title: Local merge queue for parallel coding agents
text: Lands commits from four or five parallel coding agents one at a time through a local merge queue that tests each before merging, avoiding crashes on a small laptop.

title: Twenty-plus parallel sessions improving a codebase
text: Runs twenty or more coding sessions in parallel against one codebase for bug fixing and best-practice cleanup, with lock-based coordination so agents avoid conflicting edits.

title: Multi-stage pull request review with parallel sub-agents
text: Reviews pull requests through parallel sub-agents, validation passes and persistent JSON state between stages, with an optional second opinion from another coding assistant.

title: Role-based agent team launched from one terminal
text: Launches a pre-defined team of coding agents such as planner, builder and reviewer in tmux panes, and routes or broadcasts prompts to roles from one composer.

title: Twenty agents orchestrated by a parent agent
text: Orchestrates twenty-plus coding agents across two production codebases from a parent agent in the home directory, shipping real integration work in parallel.

title: Multi-agent review compared with single-pass review
text: Compares a multi-agent code review against a single-agent pass, finding 23 of 27 serious bugs for 21 dollars in 56 minutes versus 21 bugs in 40 seconds.

title: Ten-agent swarm building a desktop app
text: Coordinates ten agents in a swarm mode that builds a macOS application in parallel, studied in a deep dive on how the swarm divides the work.

title: Issue tracker driving containerised coding sessions
text: Spawns isolated container sessions of coding agents triggered by issue assignment, where an agent plans, waits for approval, implements, opens a pull request and answers review comments.

title: Kubernetes orchestration from ticket to pull request
text: Orchestrates coding agents on a Kubernetes cluster that take tickets through to pull requests, alongside automated workflows and interactive sessions in one place.

title: Eight-specialist product team inside a terminal
text: Turns a coding session into a coordinated team of eight specialists covering design, code, QA, content, marketing, legal and research, with a project manager coordinating sprints.

title: Parallel developer teams from one request
text: Splits one request into independent tasks and spawns several developer agents to build in parallel, aiming for one-shot execution.

title: Autonomous sessions coordinated via Discord webhooks
text: Coordinates multiple autonomous coding sessions through hooks, Discord webhooks and a simple protocol, pushing mobile notifications and delivering engineering reports overnight.

title: Five-agent dev team messaging over channels
text: Spins up five coding sessions covering product, engineering, QA, marketing and analysis that message each other by alias in channels and pick up cards from a Kanban board.

title: Architect, manager and engineer agents with test gating
text: Runs a YAML-defined team where an architect plans, a manager dispatches and engineers execute in tmux panes, with tests gating each step so parallel agents stop colliding.

title: Manager agent delegating to peer-reviewing agents
text: Breaks a request into tasks, assigns coding agents, manages worktrees and merges, and has agents peer review one another's code before final human approval.

title: Message bus linking separate assistant sessions
text: Connects multiple assistant sessions through a shared message bus where each registers a name, sends messages, creates channels, shares data and waits for replies to delegate work.

title: Three-assistant review of every development phase
text: Has three different assistants review each development phase and keeps specs in git, finding that no single reviewer caught more than 55 percent of issues, across 106 pull requests in two weeks.

title: Agent-made Rust replacement for a transfer library
text: Directs coding agents to rewrite a widely used network transfer library in Rust as a largely agent-made project.

title: Online bookstore operated by one agent harness
text: Runs a small online bookstore through an agent harness that rotates its book selection every 24 hours and blogs each decision, with no fixed workflow for its goal of selling more books.

title: Four-role research pipeline with feedback loop
text: Runs four agents, researcher, analyst, writer and verifier, that collaborate through shared state and a three-way feedback loop.

title: Personal team of research agents
text: Maintains a personal team of specialised research agents as a shared repository that one person reuses for research work across several specialised roles.

title: Three agents drafting outreach for a company
text: Takes a company's URL and runs three agents, one to research, one to write and one to score, producing three scored outreach drafts in about ten seconds.

title: Parallel strategy agents with a devil's advocate
text: Runs three agents in parallel, for research, strategy and devil's advocate, over a business question and merges their output into a brief.

title: Eleven specialised agents trading crypto and forex
text: Operates eleven specialised agents as a proprietary trading firm that trades crypto and forex around the clock through a multi-agent setup.

title: Multi-agent trading on a crypto exchange
text: Coordinates several agents to analyse markets and place trades on a decentralised crypto perpetuals exchange through a multi-agent trading bot.

title: Two agents trading with markdown memory files
text: Has two agents trade with each other while each keeps its memory in a versioned markdown file, to watch what happens.

title: Multi-agent workflows for game development
text: Builds multi-agent workflows for making games across Unity, Godot, web and mini-game engines, with specialised agents handling parts of the game development process.

title: Pixel-art control room for agents
text: Shows a coding team's agents as characters in a pixel-art mission control, growing toward an agent-run company.

title: Tmux swarm with task scheduling
text: Schedules tasks across multiple coding sessions in tmux so agents execute concurrently on one project.

title: Three-tier swarm for find-me-X searches
text: Runs a three-tier swarm of discovery, search and grading agents for open-ended sourcing jobs such as niches and suppliers.

title: Measuring whether extra agents earn their keep
text: Runs one agent, then a swarm, on the same task and measures whether the additional agents improved the result.

title: Swarm resolving GitHub issues autonomously
text: Runs an autonomous swarm of coding sessions that picks up GitHub issues and works them in parallel.

title: Novel-writing plugin with multiple agents
text: Splits novel writing among multiple specialised agents inside a coding assistant plugin, so different agents handle different parts of the writing job.

title: Six sessions improvising as a jam band
text: Has six coding sessions play together as a jam band, each contributing to the music.

title: Lead and teammates in separate contexts
text: Uses a team lead that coordinates teammates working in independent contexts, via an experimental agent teams feature of a coding assistant.

title: Plan, spec, execute, verify, fix pipeline
text: Chains three agents through plan, spec, execute, verify and fix stages with no human in the review queue, in a widely starred orchestration layer.

title: Tmux colony of collaborating coding instances
text: Runs multiple coding instances in tmux that collaborate on software tasks, building on a coding assistant's native subagent definitions.

title: Telegram-routed named agents in containers
text: Routes Telegram messages to named agents, each running in its own isolated Docker container, with a real-time web control room for a personal assistant.

title: Ten coding sessions managed side by side
text: Runs ten coding sessions at once from a desktop app that keeps every session accessible, so one person drives a team of agents.

title: Orchestrator delegating to coding agents and reviewers
text: Hands software work to an orchestrator that plans it, starts several coding agents, has other agents review and check the result, and reports back.

title: Nine agents debating across forum threads
text: Lets nine autonomous agents from several vendors hold discussions in forum threads, producing 259 threads and 2,468 posts in an archive.

title: Issue-to-verified-pull-request autonomous loop
text: Turns a task or issue into a verified pull request through coordinated autonomous agents that attach a signed receipt of the checks.

title: Meta-harness running swarms of coding agents
text: Coordinates swarms of coding agents across two coding assistants through a meta-harness for large engineering tasks.

title: Experiment coordinating sessions with shared notes
text: Coordinates several coding sessions on a local project while showing their tasks, terminal output and shared notes in a dashboard.

title: Multi-model code review with Codex and Gemini
text: Orchestrates several coding assistants as reviewers on a task to gather diverse perspectives, then compares their findings.

title: Shared chat room for humans and coding agents
text: Puts team members and several coding agents in one shared chat room that routes each message to the right agent.
